sections.heading: How to turn a recording into notes
sections.body:
Start with a recording you already have. It can be an audio file or a video file. The tool listens to the recording and writes notes in the style you choose.

1. Open [Audio to Notes](https://audio-to-notes.lazur.app/).
2. Choose your recording. Audio and video both work, as long as the file is 15 MB or smaller.
3. Pick a notes style: Short summary + bullet points, Detailed notes, or Action items only.
4. Wait for the result. Most answers come back in about 1 to 3 seconds. Video files take longer.
5. Read the notes, then copy them with one click.

The notes start with a one-line title, so you can tell one set of notes from another later.

The tool is built for speech. A recording with music in the background, or a mix of many voices talking at once, gives notes that are harder to follow, so a clean recording of one speaker or a few speakers works best.

sections.heading: Pick the style that fits the recording
sections.body:
**Short summary + bullet points** gives you the main idea and a short list of key points. It is the quickest read after a podcast or a voice memo.

Detailed notes keep more of what was said, in the order it was said. Use it for a lecture, an interview or a call where the details matter.

Action items only pulls out the tasks and next steps. Use it after a meeting when you need a to-do list, not the whole discussion.

You can run the same recording again with a different style. Each run counts toward your free runs for the day.

sections.heading: Limits to know before you start
sections.body:
The tool takes files up to 15 MB. A bigger file will not be accepted, so check the file size in your file manager before you upload. If the file is too large, cut out the part you need and upload that.

You get 3 free runs a day. After you leave an email, you get 3 more. You do not need an account to start.

sections.heading: Check the notes against the recording
sections.body:
Notes are only as clear as the audio. A quiet room, a fan or a crowd of voices can make the notes weaker. Names, numbers and technical words are the parts most worth checking. Play the spot where a number or a name comes up and compare it with the notes before you use them.

If you take notes by voice every day, Lazur does this on your Mac: hold two keys and talk, and it types the result into whatever app you are in.

pages.title: How to Take Notes From Audio, Step by Step | Lazur
pages.description: Two easy ways to take notes from audio: turn a recording you already have into notes, or record and transcribe on an iPhone in the Notes app.
pages.h1: How to take notes from audio
pages.claim: Upload a recording you already have and the tool writes notes in the style you pick. To take notes while you record on an iPhone, use Notes: tap Attachments, then Record Audio, then tap Record.

sections.heading: Option 1: notes from a recording you already have
sections.body:
Use this option when the audio file already exists, such as a voice memo, a lecture or a podcast episode.

1. Open [Audio to Notes](https://audio-to-notes.lazur.app/take-from).
2. Choose the audio or video file. It must be 15 MB or smaller.
3. Pick a notes style: Short summary + bullet points, Detailed notes, or Action items only.
4. Wait for the notes. Most come back in about 1 to 3 seconds.
5. Copy the notes with one click and paste them where you keep your notes.

This tool works on a file you already have. It does not record, so record first and upload when you are done.

Pick the style before you start. If the recording is an hour of class, Detailed notes gives you the most to work with. If it is a two-minute voice memo to yourself, Short summary + bullet points is enough. Check the result against the audio once, then keep the notes where you will look for them, such as in the same folder as the recording.

sections.heading: Option 2: take notes while you record on an iPhone
sections.body:
The Notes app on iPhone can record audio and transcribe it as you go. The steps below come from Apple's support page, [Record and transcribe audio in Notes](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/record-and-transcribe-audio-iphbe11247b5/ios).

1. Open the Notes app on your iPhone.
2. In a note, tap the Attachments button, then tap Record Audio.
3. Tap the Record button to start the recording.
4. To take notes during the recording, swipe down from the top of the screen.
5. When you finish, tap the Pause button, then tap Done.

After you record, the More button in the recording's playback lets you add the transcript to the note or copy it.

sections.heading: Which option to use
sections.body:
Use Notes on iPhone when you are recording and want to write as you listen, with the live transcript on screen. Use Audio to Notes when the recording is already made and you want the main points or a to-do list pulled out of it. Once you have the notes, paste them into the app where you keep your work, and check the names and numbers against the audio, because one wrong digit can change the meaning. The two can work together: record in Notes during the class or call, then upload the finished recording here if you want a second set of notes in a different style.

**Keep the recording.** Notes are only as good as the audio, so save the original file until you have checked the notes against it.

faq.q: How do I take audio notes on an iPhone?
faq.a: Open Notes, tap the Attachments button in a note, and tap Record Audio. Tap Record to start, then tap Pause and Done when you finish. To make notes from a recording you already have, use Audio to Notes instead.

faq.q: Can I take notes from an audio file for free?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the file to Audio to Notes and choose a notes style. You get 3 free runs a day, and 3 more after you leave an email. No account is needed.

faq.q: Can I take notes while I record?
faq.a: Use the recording feature of your app, such as Notes on an iPhone, to record and watch the live transcript. Audio to Notes works on a recording that already exists, so upload it once the recording is finished.

faq.q: Why are my notes missing details?
faq.a: The notes follow the style you picked. Choose Detailed notes to keep more of what was said. Quiet or noisy audio also makes notes weaker, so try a clearer recording if the result is thin.
